sharedBitmapCore.reuse: The physical ABI adapter and borrowed resources invoke the same CRLF framing, BDF token/line parser, header/glyph scanner, Thai property parser, bitmap decoder, icon directory lookup and packed-bit coverage core. Native state layouts, paged workspace serialization, keyword numbers, physical addresses, engine configuration and callbacks stay in the adapter.
sharedBitmapCore.baseline: baseline(&self)->PixelOffset; BDF is header BBX height plus y offset, DCW is zero
sharedBitmapCore.bearing: The shared mask bearing is relative to a baseline pen. BDF bearing_y is -glyph BBX y offset minus glyph height. The physical adapter separately adds the font baseline to preserve its font-top argument. DCW takes its caller y directly.
sharedBitmapCore.coverage: BDF returns PackedMsb1 and rejects other requested encodings. DCW returns a borrowed PackedMsb1 mask or expands into caller workspace as Gray4 bytes 0/15 or Gray8 bytes 0/255. No bitmap scaling is introduced.
sharedBitmapCore.ownership: Resources borrow validated bytes. BDF masks borrow the supplied decoded workspace. DCW packed masks borrow the resource; expanded masks borrow caller workspace. No heap allocation, fake initialized state, desired-values provider or GVFF equivalence.
sharedBitmapCore.sealedMask: Producers use crate-private GlyphMask::from_renderer after producing source-defined packed or gray samples. DCW Gray4 expansion emits only zero or fifteen, so no second range scan is performed. Public GlyphMask::new validates active Gray4 samples, ignores stride padding and exposes read-only getters.
sharedBitmapCore.constructorOwner: PipelineTransforms owns src/font_core.rs and font_core/resource.rs, including FontAsset::parse and FontEngine::new
sharedBitmapCore.consumerOwner: GraphicsRuntime.GraphicsCpuRaster owns Surface::draw_glyph_mask(baseline,mask,colour) and the cross-family consumer fixtures
sharedBitmapCore.behavioralFixtures: Seven tests in bitmap.rs exercise real FontAsset/FontEngine construction from independent literal CRLF BDF and DCW ICON resources, literal metrics and packed/gray pixels, missing glyph/workspace/invalid-resource errors, and public Gray4 mask range validation with stride padding. Original/native ABI scenarios retain their interfaces; Thai name-padding fixtures are corrected and extended from A32 word-comparison evidence.
sharedBitmapCore.qualification: Source-only. No builds, tests, native runs, formatters or SDK/guest setup performed. Joint producer/consumer qualification remains the integration owner's gate.

headerRelativeToState.12: font bounding box width,height,x,y signed halfwords

iconResource.34: page-count pairs of high code byte and directory slot byte
iconResource.glyphOffset: directory little-endian word, zero absent; otherwise resource + 32 + offset
iconResource.glyph: width byte, height byte, then MSB-first rows with ceil(width/8) bytes; not GVFF

behavior.bdf: CRLF line framing; header CHARS terminates header scan. STARTPROPERTIES skips its declared line count. Glyph BITMAP records the text offset and skips height equal-length rows before ENDCHAR. Index uses a 256-word high-page directory and 256-word glyph pages. Initialization checks workspace size before state writes and compares indexed glyph count after writes.
behavior.parser: Keyword dispatch uses token length plus its first four bytes; length-three tokens take BBX, length-nine tokens distinguish STARTCHAR by byte five. Decimal accumulation wraps and halfword fields retain low sixteen bits. No new validation is introduced.
behavior.bdfDrawing: Missing glyph returns zero. Parse failure can invoke the engine fallback. Direct packed decode applies when engine text format is one and final x is zero. Scratch path checks byte capacity before fill and decode, merges set bits only for format bit 0x100, then translates and clears the optional rectangle. Return is raw DWIDTH, without engine bias.
behavior.iconDrawing: Returns glyph width plus engine bias after drawing or format suppression. Packed aligned path indexes destination by y*stride+x exactly as original, while unaligned path indexes y*stride+(x>>3) and writes the spill byte. No last-byte mask is added. Coverage bit 0x200 expands set bits and ORs either 15 or 255 according to engine depth/options. Optional mode-one extra sets row count before destination height clipping.
behavior.padding: BDF padding outputs are independently nullable; icon padding writes all four unconditionally.

nativeThaiNamePadding.evidence: A32 0x1190e50..0x1190e80, 0x1190f24..0x1190f54 and 0x1190ff8..0x1191024 compare all three name words for nine/ten-byte names, including zero padding through byte eleven. THAI_TOP compares only its first eight bytes.
nativeThaiNamePadding.adapter: Logical Thai property parsing is shared; the native adapter applies the original padded-word guard before writing output fields.
nativeThaiNamePadding.fixtureInference: [INFERENCE] STARTPROPERTIES leaves nonzero bytes ten/eleven in token scratch, so the literal properties fixture updates THAI_TOP but leaves THAI_BASE unchanged. The two-property-lines fixture starts with zeroed scratch and updates both.

preconditions: Original ABI pointers name readable/writable mapped objects for the complete accessed extent and remain live for the call.
Text resources have CRLF framing and the original parser grammar; caller supplies scratch and a zeroed glyph index. These raw entries take no resource byte length.
Glyph index high-page and glyph offsets address the supplied text resource. Resources and output buffers do not overlap.
Owner engine pointers and their configuration/span/workspace objects are installed by the canonical frontend.
No concurrent engine mutation occurs during a backend call.
